facebook.content_angle: Six-beat kick efficiency — how most competitive swimmers use a two-beat kick and bleed speed across every length without realising it, with the drill fix that delivered 10.21% improvement in 50m times
facebook.post_text:
Most swimmers are racing with the handbrake on. 🚨

If you're still running a two-beat kick in freestyle, you're leaving measurable speed in the water on every single length — not occasionally. Every length.

👉 A two-beat kick drops your leg drive between strokes, sinks your hips, and forces your arms to compensate for the drag your lower body is creating.
👉 Elite freestyle is built on a six-beat kick cycle — six leg strikes per full arm stroke — creating a continuous propulsive rhythm that keeps your body line flat and your speed consistent.
👉 Swimmers who switched to a structured six-beat kick pattern recorded a 10.21% improvement in 50m times within four weeks of consistent drill work.

This is the autumn block. The metres you put in now at training pace determine what the clock says in spring. ⏱️

✔️ Drill it: 6-beat kick on kickboard, 25m sets, count every strike
✔️ Transfer it: build the rhythm into full-stroke repeats at race pace
✔️ Own it: the kick that feels foreign in week one becomes automatic by week four

Are you running a six-beat kick — or guessing?
facebook.engagement_bait: Drop a 2️⃣ if you've never been coached on kick count, or a 6️⃣ if you're already drilling it.
